The last solar eclipse before the year 2000 occurred on **August 11, 1999**. It was a **total solar eclipse**, visible across a path stretching from the Atlantic Ocean through the UK (southern Cornwall), France, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, Hungary, Yugoslavia (now Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina), Bulgaria, Turkey, Syria, Iraq, Iran, Pakistan, India, and ending in Bangladesh and the Bay of Bengal.

This was the final solar eclipse of the 20th century, and the last one before January 1, 2000.

✅ Confirmed via NASA’s official eclipse catalog (NASA Eclipse Web Site, Fred Espenak).  
Note: There were no solar eclipses in December 1999 — the next one after August 11, 1999, was on **July 31, 2000**, but that was *after* the year 2000 began.

So, the answer is: **August 11, 1999**.
